top.headline: Iran vows to break US blockade as Hormuz standoff turns hotter
top.summary: Tehran says it will use every means available against the US naval blockade, and more tankers have been reported on fire in the strait while Trump threatens to sink Iranian ships. Iran says Hormuz could reopen within two days if Washington halts hostilities, lifts the blockade and waives sanctions.

top.headline: Tech-led rout puts the Nasdaq 100 near a bear market
top.summary: The S&P 500 and Dow slid into correction last week as investors dumped tech, and the selloff is spreading to metals and emerging markets. Dip buyers are hesitating, though Goldman's desk sees an entry point.

top.headline: COP31 collapses after nations reject a fossil-friendly deal
top.summary: UN climate talks ended without a major agreement after the EU and others refused a draft they said walked back earlier commitments to move away from fossil fuels. The failure leaves the energy-transition path murkier heading into 2027.

stories.headline: Traders brace for another volatile week after the tech rout
stories.body: Wall Street starts the week under pressure after a sharp rotation out of US stocks, with the S&P 500 and Dow now in correction. The Nasdaq 100 is close to bear-market territory and contrarian buyers are holding back. Options traders are positioning for more swings as the AI trade falters.
stories.why: A broad de-risking like this tends to hit Gulf and emerging-market equities and tighten financing conditions everywhere.

stories.headline: Fed hike bets collide with falling stocks; Bessent warns of overtightening
stories.body: Bond investors have been betting the Fed will raise rates to fight inflation, but the equity slide is muddying that trade. Treasury Secretary Bessent warned the Fed could damage the economy by tightening too far after the latest inflation figures.
stories.why: The rate path drives the dollar, and with it the cost of money in dollar-pegged Gulf economies like Qatar.

stories.headline: Turmoil spreads to metals and emerging markets; Asia braces
stories.body: US stock futures opened slightly higher, but the selloff has spilled into metals and EM assets, and Asia-Pacific markets were set for losses at the open. Goldman's trading desk sees a possible entry point but warns positioning is still stretched.
stories.why: Watch for contagion into GCC markets and EM debt, where Gulf sovereign funds are active buyers.

stories.headline: Yardeni trims S&P 500 target again but rules out a bear market
stories.body: Strategist Ed Yardeni cut his year-end S&P 500 forecast for the second time in roughly two months. He still expects the market to avoid a full bear market.
stories.why: One of Wall Street's steadiest bulls turning more cautious is a useful read on sentiment.

stories.headline: Oil edges lower as ample supply outweighs Gulf escalation
stories.body: Crude slipped as strong exports from other producers offset the risk from the escalating Hormuz confrontation. The market is treating supply as plentiful despite the war.
stories.why: Soft prices alongside a Gulf war squeeze GCC budgets while offering little relief to importers.

stories.headline: EU explains why it walked away from the UN climate deal
stories.body: The EU's chief negotiator said the draft would have weakened earlier commitments on transitioning away from fossil fuels. Talks ended in acrimony with no major agreement.
stories.why: No new global push away from fossil fuels supports long-term demand for Gulf oil and gas, but leaves policy uncertainty for buyers.

stories.headline: Europe's power market flashes a warning
stories.body: German steelmakers are facing hours when electricity is too expensive to run plants. High energy prices are also feeding a stagflation shock in the Czech Republic, according to one of its central bankers.
stories.why: Europe's energy stress keeps demand for LNG high, which matters for Qatar once its exports recover.

stories.headline: Australia's gas reservation plan faces a vote this week
stories.body: The opposition is demanding changes to a plan that would reserve part of LNG output for the domestic market, ahead of a parliamentary vote this week.
stories.why: Australia is a key rival to Qatar in Asian LNG; curbs on its exports would tighten supply further.

stories.headline: Ukraine says it struck Russian ships off Libya
stories.body: Zelenskyy said Ukrainian sea drones were behind attacks on Russian vessels near Libya, including at Benghazi port, and claimed the warship Merkury was sunk. The strikes raise fears the war is spreading to the Mediterranean.
stories.why: A wider maritime war adds to shipping and insurance risk on routes already strained by Hormuz and the Red Sea.

stories.headline: At least 15 killed as Russia steps up attacks around Kyiv
stories.body: The death toll from Russian strikes in the Kyiv region has risen to at least 15. The attacks come even as the UAE has hosted rounds of US-Russia-Ukraine peace talks.
stories.why: Escalation on both sides lowers the odds of a near-term deal that would ease energy markets.

stories.headline: After the Trump-Xi-Putin summit, smaller powers take stock
stories.body: Last week's three-way summit in Shenzhen sent a less reassuring message to middle powers like Singapore, Bloomberg's analysis argues. Some commentators see it as the formal arrival of a great-power order.
stories.why: Gulf states have built their strategy on balancing between the big powers, which gets harder if those powers deal over their heads.

stories.headline: US-China tech friction widens
stories.body: US intelligence says it is investigating an alleged Chinese spy linked to Nvidia's former CEO, and Beijing has objected to US curbs on three Chinese telecoms. New US chip rules are also squeezing Southeast Asia's cloud and data-centre boom.
stories.why: Chip export rules shape where AI capacity gets built, including the Gulf's own data-centre ambitions.

stories.headline: Europe's autumn of protest: Belgium strikes, France's students march
stories.body: A national anti-austerity strike snarled transport across Belgium, while French students are protesting nationwide. In Spain, conservative Alberto Feijóo is bidding to become prime minister.
stories.why: Political pressure against austerity makes Europe's fiscal outlook, and its bond markets, harder to read.

stories.headline: Anthropic slides after the biggest IPO ever
stories.body: Anthropic raised $81.3bn at a $1.5tn valuation, pricing shares at $83 and overtaking SpaceX's record. Its stock then fell, failing to calm fears of an AI bubble and dragging on Asian markets.
stories.why: The AI trade's health drives tech valuations globally, and Gulf funds are major backers of AI ventures.

stories.headline: Calls grow for limits on frontier AI
stories.body: OpenAI's chief scientist urged the industry to limit building more powerful models until monitoring improves, and a bipartisan group of US governors called for federal AI rules that still let states protect consumers. A senior Meta executive warned that superintelligence is arriving.
stories.why: Regulation risk is now part of the case for and against AI stocks, and it is one reason they are selling off.

stories.headline: Deals: Compass eyes New York, Ashland and Quotient in play
stories.body: UK caterer Compass Group plans to move its primary listing from London to New York, the FT reports. Clariant and CD&R are in talks to buy $3.3bn chemicals firm Ashland, and IQVIA is close to a roughly $1.1bn takeover of Quotient Sciences.
stories.why: Compass leaving is another blow to London as a listing venue; deal flow is holding up despite the selloff.

stories.headline: Nvidia's scandal opens a door for India's AI players
stories.body: With Nvidia caught up in a spy scandal and US chip rules tightening, Indian groups are pitching themselves as alternative AI hubs.
stories.why: Competition for AI investment is heating up, and the Gulf is competing for the same capital.

stories.headline: The blockade, month by month
stories.body: The US first blockaded Iran in April, lifted it in June after a draft understanding, and reimposed it on 14 July when that deal collapsed, later adding sanctions and a task force against land routes. Visible Iranian crude exports are near zero. Iran has held talks with Qatari mediators, though diplomacy remains stalled.
stories.why: Doha is both a mediator and one of the economies most exposed to how this ends.

stories.headline: Qatar's LNG still largely trapped behind Hormuz
stories.body: Qatari LNG loadings recovered to around half of pre-war levels in November, despite an attack on one of its tankers in late October. QatarEnergy has extended force majeure on some Asian and European deliveries through the end of November.
stories.why: LNG is the backbone of Qatar's economy, and every month of disruption pushes buyers toward US and other suppliers.

stories.headline: Blockade is pushing up Gulf insurance premiums
stories.body: A US maritime agency warned that the blockade was adding to rising insurance costs for shipping in the Gulf, according to an Al Jazeera exclusive.
stories.why: Higher war-risk premiums raise the cost of every cargo moving in and out of Gulf ports.

stories.headline: Houthi war with Saudi Arabia heats up
stories.body: Saudi civil defence confirmed several floors of the PIF Tower in Riyadh's financial district were damaged in a Houthi attack, with no injuries. Heavy fighting is reported on several Yemeni fronts, and Bloomberg examines why the Houthis have proved so hard to defeat.
stories.why: Attacks reaching Riyadh's financial heart raise risk for Gulf investment and aviation.

stories.headline: Saudi oil exports rebound via the Red Sea
stories.body: Saudi crude and product exports have averaged about 8.57m barrels a day so far this quarter, around 37% above the third quarter, according to Vortexa data cited by Asharq. Roughly 2.5m bpd is moving through Red Sea ports, avoiding Hormuz.
stories.why: Pipelines that bypass Hormuz are a big advantage for Saudi Arabia and the UAE; Qatar's LNG has no such route.

stories.headline: Why the tech rout hits your whole portfolio at once
stories.body: All seven holdings are tied to the AI and software trade that is now selling off, with the Nasdaq 100 close to bear-market territory. SPUS doesn't spread the risk much either: the Sharia-screened S&P 500 fund is weighted about 38% to electronic technology and 22% to technology services, and Microsoft, Alphabet and Broadcom are among its biggest holdings.
stories.why: Your positions tend to fall together on days like this. That concentration is the biggest risk in the portfolio right now.

stories.headline: AMD drops as much as 11% on a China firmware report
stories.body: AMD fell sharply on 19 November after a Hunterbrook report about firmware and China. It comes after a volatile run: AMD climbed as investors moved money out of Nvidia during its leadership crisis, then slid with the rest of the chip sector. Q3 revenue jumped 45% to $13.4bn, and AMD guided to about $17bn for Q4.
stories.why: Strong fundamentals versus headline risk: any follow-up on the China report could move the stock quickly.

stories.headline: Microsoft teams up with Nvidia and Anthropic as analysts stay bullish
stories.body: On 18 November Microsoft announced a partnership with Nvidia and Anthropic to scale Claude on Azure. Mizuho and UBS both reiterated Buy ratings on 20 November, with targets of $640 and $650. The stock has still fallen more than 12% since its fiscal Q1 results, and a Microsoft 365 outage hit shares in mid-November.
stories.why: Microsoft is also one of SPUS's largest holdings, so its moves count twice in your portfolio.

stories.headline: Google rolls out new AI chips; shares still well off highs
stories.body: Google is introducing two new custom TPU chips to compete with Nvidia, according to Bloomberg, and the stock rose on the news. Alphabet dropped about 12.6% the day after Q3 results in late October, when search ad growth slowed and AI spending surged, and it faces a newly filed class-action lawsuit.
stories.why: TPUs give Google its own path in AI hardware; the next earnings are expected in early February.

stories.headline: Broadcom heads into 9 December earnings after a 20% slide
stories.body: Broadcom is down about 20% since the end of July after Q4 guidance came in slightly below estimates and the 5 November sell-off hit chip stocks. It bounced 9% on 9 November as buyers returned to semiconductors. Fiscal Q4 results are due on 9 December.
stories.why: Earnings in two weeks will show whether AI chip demand justifies Broadcom's valuation.

stories.headline: ServiceNow is still recovering from its worst day in years
stories.body: Q3 revenue rose 20.5% to $4.11bn, in line with forecasts, but EPS of $1.00 just missed the $1.02 consensus, and margin pressure sent the stock to its worst one-day drop in more than 14 years. ServiceNow raised its 2026 subscription revenue outlook to $15.785bn and says AI adoption is accelerating.
stories.why: The question for NOW is whether AI grows its business or disrupts it. Next earnings are expected in late January.

stories.headline: Shopify grew 32% but the market wanted more
stories.body: Q3 revenue rose about 32% to $3.74bn and adjusted EPS beat estimates, yet shares fell as much as 13% on 3 November as investors picked at operating metrics. Shopify guides to low-30s percent revenue growth in Q4 and is spending more on marketing ahead of the holidays.
stories.why: Black Friday and holiday sales over the coming weeks are the next real test of Shopify's growth.

watch.what: US session after Asia's open: does the Nasdaq 100 tip into a bear market?
Australian parliament votes on the gas reservation plan for LNG.
US Thanksgiving: Wall Street closed; thin trading into Friday.
Iran's talks with Qatari mediators, and any US response to Tehran's two-day reopening offer for Hormuz.
